evidence.label: def:p19-proposed-factorial-design: the existing 2x2 design (checking instruction x numerical aid) and its opposite-sign example (4,0,0,2): aid-present difference 2 vs equal-weight average -1; file unchanged since the root commit, so the example is preserved, not replaced

def:p15-factorial-coding: retains the P19 experiment; explicit coding x=2a-1, z=2b-1 and the coded cell-mean model; conditional effects Delta_A(0)=mu10-mu00, Delta_A(1)=mu11-mu01; equal-weight average Delta_A; Delta_B defined symmetrically; difference of differences D_AB=mu11-mu01-mu10+mu00; the D_AB/2 and D_AB/4 normalizations

thm:p15-factorial-two-by-two: analysis matrix H_2 in cell order (00,10,01,11) with H_2^T H_2=4I; Delta_A=2beta_A, Delta_B=2beta_B, D_AB=4beta_AB, Delta_A(b)=2beta_A+2(2b-1)beta_AB; zero-one coding coefficients mu00, Delta_A(0), Delta_B(0), D_AB

def:p15-factorial-retained-example: retained means (4,0,0,2): conditional checking effects -4 and 2, average -1, D_AB=6; aid effects -4 and 2, average -1; coded coefficients (3/2,-1/2,-1/2,3/2); explicit solutions a of H_2^T a=c; missing-cell nonidentification; the sign difference is retained
annex:p15.factorial.two-by-two: written derivation of orthogonality, the conditional effect, averaging, differencing to 4beta_AB, the zero-one expansion and the numerical values

sec:p15-factorial-full: def:p15-factorial-walsh and thm:p15-factorial-walsh with the source's Table 3.4 analysis matrix and replicated responses; checked against the held PDF Table 3.2 (p.1320) and Table 3.4 (pp.1322-1323), and the 2^2 base with its X1*X2 column (Tables 3.12-3.13, p.1336) at lines 538-547
thm:p15-factorial-estimability: repeating existing design rows does not change which targets are estimable (proof annex:p15.factorial.estimability, annex lines 21-24)

sec:p15-factorial-uncertainty: thm:p15-factorial-linear-uncertainty (residual space of dimension N-r, s^2=SSE/(N-r) unbiased, exact Student interval) and thm:p15-factorial-joint-test; a zero residual degree of freedom supplies no variance estimate

thm:p15-factorial-replication: cell mean variance sigma^2/n_j; pure-error sum of squares with expectation (N-m)sigma^2; SSE = pure error + lack of fit; repeated measurements on one unit have variance sigma_U^2+sigma_e^2/q; four task answers from one participant are not four independently randomized participants

sec:p15-factorial-randomized-blocks: source CRD (90 and 369600 sequences, displayed sequence 3,1,4,2,2,1,3,4,1,2,4,3; held PDF pp.1300-1302) and wafer complete-block example (held PDF pp.1304-1306); thm:p15-factorial-blocks: zero-sum treatment contrasts eliminate every additive block effect, variance sigma^2*sum(c_t^2)/B, residual df (L-1)(B-1), interaction not separable from pure error with one observation per cell
thm:p15-factorial-walsh and the replicated Table 3.4 example: variance sigma^2/(n 2^k), 2^k(n-1) pure-error df; pure-error SS 5 on 8 df, s^2=5/8, effect standard error sqrt(5/32)

sec:p15-factorial-execution: randomized run order and centre points of Tables 3.5-3.9 (held PDF pp.1324-1328); thm:p15-factorial-centers-blocks: the block column equals the 123 column (Table 3.10, held PDF pp.1329-1331), only gamma+beta_123 is identified, centres run in both blocks separate them under the enlarged model; within-block replication keeps its own assignment unit
annex:p15.factorial.linear-uncertainty: residual trace identity and the Student pivot

annex:p15.factorial.replication and annex:p15.factorial.blocks: written proofs of pure-error expectation, the SSE decomposition, the clustered variance, block-effect cancellation, the variance and the residual dimension
annex:p15.factorial.walsh: replicated-example computation of cell means, pure-error SS 5 and variance estimate 5/32
annex:p15.factorial.centers-blocks: block/123 alias and the centre-point separation
def:p15-factorial-fraction and thm:p15-factorial-alias: regular fraction, run count 2^(k-p), exact alias relation, alias-sum expectation of a fraction contrast

sec:p15-factorial-half: 2^(3-1) construction from the 2^2 base (source Tables 3.12-3.15, held PDF pp.1336-1337); alias classes I=123, 1=23, 2=13, 3=12 (source 5.3.3.4.3, held PDF pp.1339-1340); columns x3 and x1x2 coincide; (beta3+t, beta12-t) leaves every fitted response unchanged; only their sum is recovered; negative fraction signs reversed

def:p15-factorial-nist-effects: source responses (33,63,41,57,57,51,59,53) (Table 3.11, held PDF pp.1333-1335); fraction contrasts (8,16,10) equal the predicted alias differences of full-factorial effects; principal fraction (9,-13,3); fractions estimate different sums
thm:p15-factorial-estimability: a non-estimable target gives two parameter values with the same observation law
annex:p15.factorial.alias: written proof of the alias relation; the principal-fraction alias classes; adding t(e_3-e_12) changes neither the fitted values nor the observation law

sec:p15-factorial-causal: def:p15-factorial-assignment and thm:p15-factorial-assignment: the assignment contrast tau with fixed weights, its unbiased weighting estimator (equal to sum w_t Ybar_t under complete randomization), exact randomization variance; P19 weights (0,0,-1,1) and (-1,1,-1,1)/2, which are the estimability solutions a of lines 107-110; premises (versions, consistency, interference, missingness, noncompliance, sampling/transport)

thm:p15-factorial-mechanism: complete estimation of the factorial surface 4-4A-4B+6AB does not identify the reflection mechanism; the additional premise for a mechanism claim: process measurements with an explicit measurement model, interventions or controls separating the competing mechanisms, and assumptions connecting those observations to the causal equations; estimability, uncertainty, assignment effect and mechanism each have their own premises
annex:p15.factorial.assignment and annex:p15.factorial.mechanism: written proofs; the two structural models (R=A,E=0 vs R=0,E=A) agree under every assignment intervention and differ under do(R=1)
thm:p15-w02b-p15-077-correspondence: tau equals a combination of intervention means do(V_0=t1) of the structural model of the experiment
thm:p15-w02b-p15-077-identification: the assignment contrast is identified from the assigned-arm law in C_NI; unbiased estimator; complete-randomization form

def:p15-w02b-p15-077-study-premises, thm:p15-w02b-p15-077-study-contrasts and def:p15-w02b-p15-077-limits: the warranted target is the assignment contrast in the recruited sample under listed premises; a mechanism claim needs the additional evidence stated after thm:p15-factorial-mechanism; the identified quantity is not a statement about the process
annex:p15-w02b-p15-077-ident: written identification proof
annex:p15-w02b-p15-077-study: the two declared P19 contrasts identified and unbiased

def:p19-proposed-factorial-design: the design supports a comparison of the effects of assignment; a detected assignment effect does not by itself prove that reflection caused it (effort, caution, time or interpretation); process measures and alternative controls supply further evidence

defect_observations.observation: Unflagged departure from the held source. For the alternative 2^(8-3) design (6=12345, 7=135, 8=245), held PDF p.1345 (5.3.3.4.4) says 23 of 28 two-factor interactions are confounded, 'leaving only 12, 14, 23, 27 and 34'. The handbook says exactly four are clear (12, 14, 23, 34), 24 are aliased, and 27=46 (annex lines 332-337, from I=2467). The handbook's count follows from the defining relation, but the text does not say it corrects the source. This is a fidelity note and does not change any verdict.

Hyper-Graeco-Latin 5 display: the handbook prints E13 at row 3, column 4, which follows the source run table (3,4,1,3,5). The source's own letter display (held PDF pp.1318-1319) prints E31 there, which would repeat the blocking pair of D31. The departure is not flagged. Minor.

The source's non-blocked alternative is not kept. Held PDF pp.1304-1305 runs one wafer per furnace run and says this 'would increase the experimental error' by run-to-run furnace variability. The handbook shows the gain from blocking only as the cancellation of additive block effects in the blocked design, with no explicit variance comparison against the unblocked design. C02 is not downgraded: the success condition is met by the proved elimination of block effects.

Factor B is handled by symmetry: the body says 'Define Delta_B symmetrically' (lines 71-72) and the proof says 'The same calculation with the factors exchanged proves the formulas for B'. The factor-A and interaction derivations are written out and the B values are computed in the example (line 105), so the C01 success condition is met without the B step.

In the full-column-rank case of thm:p15-factorial-linear-uncertainty, the proof leaves a check to the reader ('direct multiplication verifies the displayed expression'). None of the four components' success conditions requires this step.

Ambiguous wording: 'The last two analysis columns x3, x1x2 coincide'. The last two columns of the displayed table are the two alternative x3 columns, which are negatives of each other. The coinciding pair is named explicitly (x3 = x1x2 in the principal fraction), so the statement is still present.
The 2^(6-2) remark in the source's 5.3.3.4.3 is not kept: 5=123 implies 15=23 (held PDF p.1340). The general alias theorem and the resolution corollary cover it. It is not an example matrix.

This is a unit-level obligation, not a component.
